Create the video inventory field project

Source: R/inventaire_video.R
creer_projet_inventaire_video.Rd

Builds inventaire_video.gpkg (layers placettes, centres_mesures, cibles, arbres, detections, houppiers, and the read-only parcelles, ugf and projet of schema 1.2.0, see schema_inventaire_video), the per-plot DTM and CHM GeoTIFFs (rasters/<plot_id>_mnt.tif, rasters/<plot_id>_mnh.tif: Float32, 0.5 m, strips, DEFLATE without predictor, nodata -9999) and the QField project, packaged as a .qgz like create_qgis_project.

Usage

creer_projet_inventaire_video(
  placettes,
  plot_ids = NULL,
  rayon_m = 15,
  seuil_diam_cm = 7.5,
  unite_azimut = c("deg", "gr"),
  declinaison_deg = NULL,
  avec_lidar = TRUE,
  dem = NULL,
  chm = NULL,
  project_path = NULL,
  marge_m = 10,
  cvat_path = NULL,
  output_dir,
  project_name = "inventaire_video",
  region = "BFC",
  lang = "fr",
  overwrite = TRUE,
  n_workers = .iv_workers_defaut(),
  progress_callback = NULL
)

Arguments

placettes

sf POINT of the sampling plan (plot_id required).

plot_ids

Optional character vector: plots to include.

rayon_m

Plot radius (m). Default 15 (ONF LiDAR calibration plots).

seuil_diam_cm

Minimal diameter (cm). Default 7.5.

unite_azimut

"deg" or "gr".

declinaison_deg

Magnetic declination (degrees, positive towards east). NULL (default) leaves it empty (NA, never 0): Groma then computes it with WMM2025 at the plot; a value given here takes precedence.

avec_lidar

Logical. Clip DTM/CHM and segment crowns. Default TRUE; without any DTM/CHM available, a warning is raised and the project is built without rasters.

dem, chm

SpatRaster or path. When NULL, resolved from project_path with resolve_project_dem and resolve_project_chm.

project_path

Optional nemetonshiny project directory, used to resolve dem and chm, and read (never written) to fill the tables shown by the Groma map and project list: projet (one row, from metadata.json, data/parcels.gpkg, data/commune.gpkg and the written plots; emprise is the plots' envelope in EPSG:4326 WKT), parcelles (copy of data/parcels.gpkg) and ugf (data/tenements.gpkg merged by ug_id, attributes from data/ugs.json). Without it, or when a source cannot be read (warning), those tables are created empty.

marge_m

Margin around the plot for the per-plot rasters (m), and around the plots in the forest extent when there is neither ugf nor parcelles. Default 10.

cvat_path

Optional path of a CVAT relief raster (as computed by nemetonshiny with foretaccess::vat_combined()). When given, it is cropped to the forest extent and written as rasters/cvat.tif (Byte, 2 m, EPSG:2154, DEFLATE, 0 = nodata), in Groma's coding. Accepted codings, recognised by the declared nodata: Byte with nodata 255 (foretaccess, relief 0 to 254) written as value + 1, 255 giving 0; Byte with nodata 0 (already Groma, 1 to 255) copied as is; a float relief v in \([0, 1]\) (cache of generate_rvt()) written as 1 + round(v * 254), NA giving 0. Whatever the resolution or CRS, the nodata is set to NA first, then the raster is reprojected (when not in EPSG:2154) and resampled to the 2 m grid (nearest neighbour for Byte, bilinear for float), then coded. This is a deliberate departure from section 2.3 of the Groma brief, which refused any resolution other than 2 m: the CVAT of nemetonshiny keeps the resolution of the DTM (often 0.5 m), and refusing it would break real use. Known limit: foretaccess::vat_combined(as_byte = TRUE) codes 0 to 255 with NA as 255; a valid maximal relief pixel (\(v \ge 0.996\)) is therefore indistinguishable from nodata and becomes 0 (fix planned in foretaccess). NULL (default): no cvat.tif. A missing file only raises a warning; an unreadable or otherwise coded file (Byte without nodata 0 or 255 declared, Int16, float outside \([0, 1]\)) is an error of class nemeton_erreur_cvat_codage, raised before anything is written.

output_dir

Destination directory.

project_name

File name of the .qgz (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$). Default "inventaire_video".

region, lang

Unused for the species list (the tree species list is the BD Foret V2 reference); kept for symmetry with create_qgis_project.

overwrite

Logical. Overwrite an existing .qgz. Default TRUE.

n_workers

Integer (\(\ge 1\)). Number of worker processes used to cut the per-plot rasters, write the 1 km DTM tiles and segment the crowns tile by tile. Default getOption("nemeton.iv_workers", min(4, parallel::detectCores() - 1)) (1 when the number of cores cannot be detected). 1 works sequentially, in this process. Workers are PSOCK processes (never forks, which hang with terra), started once per call and shared by the three stages, then closed; each one reads the rasters from their files, so a stage runs in parallel only when its rasters (DTM and CHM for the plots, DTM for the tiles, CHM for the crowns) are files (a path, or a SpatRaster backed by one file already in EPSG:2154); an in-memory or reprojected raster is processed sequentially. The output is identical whatever n_workers (same files and values, same topo attributes, same crown rows, order and houppier_id). If the cluster cannot be started, or a stage fails midway, a warning is raised and that stage runs sequentially.

progress_callback

Optional function called with a single list list(etape, i, n, secondes) at the start of each stage (i = 0) and after each of its units, never fatal (an error raised by the callback is ignored). etape is the stable stage name, i the units done out of n, secondes the time elapsed since the stage started (so the last call of a stage, with i == n, gives its duration). Stages, in order: "sources" (project tables and forest extent; n = 1), "placettes" (per-plot rasters and topography; n = plots), "dalles_mnt" (1 km DTM tiles; n = tiles), "houppiers" (crown segmentation; n = 1 km tiles). Each of these three stages counts per unit when sequential and per batch of n_workers units when parallel; if a parallel run fails midway and falls back to sequential, the stage restarts with a new i = 0 call and secondes restarts from 0, "cvat" (n = 1), "geopackage" (layers, triggers, indexes; n = 1) and "qgz" (.qgs, archive and project folder; n = 1). "placettes", "dalles_mnt" and "houppiers" occur only with avec_lidar (the last two also need a DTM, respectively a CHM); "cvat" only with cvat_path.

Value

Absolute path to the .qgz (invisibly). The Groma QField project plugin is written next to it as <project_name>.qml (copy of inst/inventaire_video/inventaire_video.qml, not inside the archive): ship both files to the phone. A folder <project_name>/ is also written next to the .qgz, holding the same project ready to open (<project_name>.qgs, inventaire_video.gpkg, rasters/, <project_name>.qml): QGIS resolves the ./ paths of the project from the folder of the .qgz, so a .qgz opened alone finds none of its layers. The folder is replaced like the .qgz (overwrite), edits made in it included.

Details

placettes, arbres and detections are written without spatial index: the GDAL R*Tree triggers call ST_IsEmpty on every UPDATE, a function the Android SQLite used by Groma does not know. The triggers of declencheurs.sql then link detections (written by Groma only) to arbres by uuid, without any spatial function.

The planned position and the sampling-design columns of placettes are never modified. convergence_deg (meridian convergence at the planned point) is computed; pente_pct, exposition and recouvrement_pct are filled from the DTM/CHM when empty. Crowns come from segment_houppiers over the whole forest extent (see section “Forest-wide data”), not only around the plots.

Forest-wide data (schema 1.7.0)

The forest extent is the union of the ugf plus 50 m (else of the parcelles plus 50 m, else the plots plus rayon_m + marge_m); it always also covers every plot plus rayon_m + marge_m, so that a plot planned outside the ugf keeps its data. On that extent the function writes 1 km DTM tiles rasters/mnt_<x>_<y>.tif (south-west corner in km, 4 digits; 0.5 m, same format as the per-plot rasters, nodata outside the extent or the LiDAR; no CHM tile), segments the crowns (segment_houppiers, tile by tile, a crown kept by the tile that holds its apex) and writes them to houppiers with x_sommet / y_sommet. A crown touching the buffer (rayon_m + marge_m) of one or several plots is written once per plot touched, with that plot_id (as before schema 1.7.0); a crown touching none is written once with plot_id NULL. houppier_id identifies the crown: the rows of a crown shared by two plots carry the same houppier_id. Tiles and cvat.tif (legend group "Rasters des placettes") are in the .qgz and in the project folder.
